/-!
# Erdős Problem 867

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/867](https://www.erdosproblems.com/867)
- [CoPh96] Coppersmith, Don and Phillips, Steven, *On a question of Erdős on subsequence sums*.
  SIAM J. Discrete Math. (1996), 173-177.
- [Fr93] Freud, R., *Adding numbers - on a problem of P. Erdős*. James Cook Mathematical
  Notes (1993), 6199-6202.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos867

/-- A finite set of naturals $A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_t\}$ is *consecutive-sum-free* if it has no
solutions to $a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j\in A$ with $i<j$; equivalently, whenever an interval
$[m,n]$ contains at least two elements of $A$, the sum of the elements of $A$ lying in
$[m,n]$ is not itself an element of $A$. -/
def ConsecutiveSumFree (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ m n : ℕ, 2 ≤ (Finset.Icc m n ∩ A).card → (∑ a ∈ Finset.Icc m n ∩ A, a) ∉ A

/--
Is it true that if $A=\{a_1<\cdots <a_t\}\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has no solutions to
$$a_i+a_{i+1}+\cdots+a_j\in A$$
then
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \frac{N}{2}+O(1)?$$

In fact this problem is false. Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos867.lean"]
theorem erdos_867 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / 2 + C := by
  sorry

/--
Taking $A=(N/2,N]\cap \mathbb{N}$ shows $\lvert A\rvert \geq N/2-O(1)$ is possible.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((N : ℝ) / 2 - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ)) := by
  -- Take `A = (N/2, N]`: any two of its elements already sum to more than `N`.
  refine ⟨0, fun N => ⟨Finset.Icc (N / 2 + 1) N, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc] at hx ⊢
    omega
  · intro m n hcard hmem
    set T := Finset.Icc m n ∩ Finset.Icc (N / 2 + 1) N with hT
    have hlow : ∀ x ∈ T, N / 2 + 1 ≤ x := by
      intro x hx
      simp only [hT, Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_Icc] at hx
      omega
    have hsum : T.card * (N / 2 + 1) ≤ ∑ a ∈ T, a := by
      simpa [mul_comm] using Finset.card_nsmul_le_sum T _ _ hlow
    have h2 : 2 * (N / 2 + 1) ≤ ∑ a ∈ T, a :=
      le_trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hcard) hsum
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc] at hmem
    omega
  · rw [Nat.card_Icc, sub_zero]
    have h2 : N + 1 - (N / 2 + 1) = N - N / 2 := by omega
    rw [h2]
    have h3 : N ≤ 2 * (N - N / 2) := by omega
    have h4 : (N : ℝ) ≤ ((2 * (N - N / 2) : ℕ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast h3
    push_cast at h4
    linarith

/--
Adenwalla has observed that
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq (\tfrac{2}{3}+o(1))N.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.adenwalla (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 + ε) * (N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Freud [Fr93] constructed a sequence with density $\geq 19/36$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.freud :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      (((19 / 36 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ≤ (A.card : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\frac{13}{24}N -O(1)\leq \lvert A\rvert.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((13 / 24 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - 1 / 512) * (N : ℝ) + Real.log (N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos867

reformulations.difference: The definition uses intersections with numerical intervals instead of consecutive blocks in an increasing enumeration. CoPh96 describes forbidden triples i < j < k, whereas Lean prohibits the block sum from belonging anywhere in A.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If a_i and a_j are entries of the increasing enumeration, [a_i,a_j] ∩ A consists exactly of that consecutive block. Conversely, any interval containing at least two elements of A determines such a block by its first and last elements. In every theorem A contains only positive integers, so a block of at least two terms has sum greater than its last term; any target a_k therefore automatically has k > j. Both the indexed-block equivalence and the positive-input i < j < k equivalence were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/equiv.lean.

reformulations.difference: The uniform O(1) bound is expressed for every natural N using a real constant. The cited external disproof instead uses a natural constant in 2 * A.card ≤ N + C.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An eventual uniform bound extends to all N by enlarging C to handle the finite initial range, using A.card ≤ N. The real-constant formulation is equivalent to the external proof's natural-constant formulation: round 2C upward in one direction and divide the natural constant by two in the other. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Thus these constant and boundary conventions do not change the negative assertion.

could_not_verify: Erdos867.erdos_867: Direct verification of the problem page's precise O(1) formulation was unavailable: erdosproblems.com/867 and its forum returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The cited external proof explicitly quotes and disproves the same O(1) formulation, while CoPh96's abstract describes the original question using N/2 + 1. This access limitation is not evidence of a defect.

Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.adenwalla: The specific Adenwalla remark and attribution could not be checked against the inaccessible problem page/forum. The mathematical two-thirds asymptotic bound is consistent with, and follows from, the bounds in CoPh96's accessible abstract.

Erdos867.erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound: The accessible abstract states the upper bound with '+ log n' but does not specify the logarithm's base. The full paper was inaccessible, so the exact convention needed to confirm Real.log with coefficient one remains unverified. No evidence was found that the choice is wrong.
review.notes: Source-limited review: all seven declarations were examined, but the original problem page and full papers could not be read. The accessible CoPh96 abstract confirms the finite-sequence condition and the displayed density constants. Lean checks verified empty and singleton cases, exclusion of zero by the theorem hypotheses, real-valued coefficients, the interval/indexed equivalences, and extension of eventual O(1) bounds to all N. The supplied elementary lower-bound proof has no sorry dependencies. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, equiv.lean, and proof_checks.lean. No repository files were edited. Freud's original note was not obtained; its construction was checked indirectly through CoPh96's abstract and the cited formal proof.
